##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.LogAnalyticsWorkspace.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { LogAnalyticsWorkspace } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

LogAnalyticsWorkspace.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.LogAnalyticsWorkspace.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `addTag` <a name="addTag" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_loganalyticsworkspace.LogAnalyticsWorkspace.addTag"></a>

```typescript
public addTag(key: string, value: string): void
```

Adds a tag to this resource. The tag will be included in the Azure resource.

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_loganalyticsworkspace.LogAnalyticsWorkspace.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_loganalyticsworkspace } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_loganalyticsworkspace.LogAnalyticsWorkspace.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_loganalyticsworkspace.LogAnalyticsWorkspace.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### MetricAlert <a name="MetricAlert" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.MetricAlert"></a>

Unified Azure Metric Alert implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining full JSII compliance.

Metric Alerts monitor Azure resource metrics and trigger notifications when thresholds are breached.
They support both static thresholds and dynamic thresholds based on machine learning.

*Example*

```typescript
// Dynamic threshold alert with machine learning:
const dynamicAlert = new MetricAlert(this, "dynamic-cpu", {
  name: "vm-dynamic-cpu-alert",
  resourceGroupId: resourceGroup.id,
  severity: 2,
  scopes: [resourceGroup.id],
  targetResourceType: "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines",
  targetResourceRegion: "eastus",
  criteria: {
    type: "DynamicThreshold",
    metricName: "Percentage CPU",
    operator: "GreaterThan",
    alertSensitivity: "Medium",
    failingPeriods: {
      numberOfEvaluationPeriods: 4,
      minFailingPeriodsToAlert: 3
    },
    timeAggregation: "Average"
  },
  actions: [{
    actionGroupId: actionGroup.id
  }]
});
```

### MetricAlert <a name="MetricAlert" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_metricalert.MetricAlert"></a>

Unified Azure Metric Alert implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining full JSII compliance.

Metric Alerts monitor Azure resource metrics and trigger notifications when thresholds are breached.
They support both static thresholds and dynamic thresholds based on machine learning.

*Example*

```typescript
// Dynamic threshold alert with machine learning:
const dynamicAlert = new MetricAlert(this, "dynamic-cpu", {
  name: "vm-dynamic-cpu-alert",
  resourceGroupId: resourceGroup.id,
  severity: 2,
  scopes: [resourceGroup.id],
  targetResourceType: "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines",
  targetResourceRegion: "eastus",
  criteria: {
    type: "DynamicThreshold",
    metricName: "Percentage CPU",
    operator: "GreaterThan",
    alertSensitivity: "Medium",
    failingPeriods: {
      numberOfEvaluationPeriods: 4,
      minFailingPeriodsToAlert: 3
    },
    timeAggregation: "Average"
  },
  actions: [{
    actionGroupId: actionGroup.id
  }]
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_metricalert.MetricAlert.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_metricalert } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_metricalert.MetricAlert.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_metricalert.MetricAlert.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### NetworkGroup <a name="NetworkGroup" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkGroup"></a>

Azure Virtual Network Manager Network Group implementation.

Network Groups are logical containers for virtual networks or subnets that allow you to
apply connectivity, security, or routing configurations at scale. They are a foundational
component required by connectivity configurations, security admin configurations, and
routing configurations.

*Example*

```typescript
// Network group with explicit version pinning:
const devGroup = new NetworkGroup(this, "dev-group", {
  name: "development-vnets",
  networkManagerId: networkManager.id,
  apiVersion: "2024-05-01",
  description: "Development virtual networks"
});
```


##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkGroup.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { NetworkGroup } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

NetworkGroup.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkGroup.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### NetworkGroup <a name="NetworkGroup" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_virtualnetworkmanager.NetworkGroup"></a>

Azure Virtual Network Manager Network Group implementation.

Network Groups are logical containers for virtual networks or subnets that allow you to
apply connectivity, security, or routing configurations at scale. They are a foundational
component required by connectivity configurations, security admin configurations, and
routing configurations.

*Example*

```typescript
// Network group with explicit version pinning:
const devGroup = new NetworkGroup(this, "dev-group", {
  name: "development-vnets",
  networkManagerId: networkManager.id,
  apiVersion: "2024-05-01",
  description: "Development virtual networks"
});
```

### NetworkGroupStaticMember <a name="NetworkGroupStaticMember" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkGroupStaticMember"></a>

Azure Virtual Network Manager Network Group Static Member implementation.

Static members explicitly add virtual networks or subnets to a network group,
providing precise control over which resources receive configurations applied
to the network group. This is in contrast to dynamic membership via Azure Policy.

*Example*

```typescript
// Add a subnet to a network group:
const subnetMember = new NetworkGroupStaticMember(this, "subnet-member", {
  name: "prod-subnet1-member",
  networkGroupId: productionGroup.id,
  resourceId: subnet.id,
  apiVersion: "2024-05-01"
});
```

Adds a tag to this resource. The tag will be included in the Azure resource.

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkGroupStaticMember.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { NetworkGroupStaticMember } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

NetworkGroupStaticMember.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkGroupStaticMember.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### NetworkGroupStaticMember <a name="NetworkGroupStaticMember" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_virtualnetworkmanager.NetworkGroupStaticMember"></a>

Azure Virtual Network Manager Network Group Static Member implementation.

Static members explicitly add virtual networks or subnets to a network group,
providing precise control over which resources receive configurations applied
to the network group. This is in contrast to dynamic membership via Azure Policy.

*Example*

```typescript
// Add a subnet to a network group:
const subnetMember = new NetworkGroupStaticMember(this, "subnet-member", {
  name: "prod-subnet1-member",
  networkGroupId: productionGroup.id,
  resourceId: subnet.id,
  apiVersion: "2024-05-01"
});
```

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.

the deployed Azure resource.

construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_virtualnetworkmanager.NetworkGroupStaticMember.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_virtualnetworkmanager } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_virtualnetworkmanager.NetworkGroupStaticMember.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_virtualnetworkmanager.NetworkGroupStaticMember.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### NetworkInterface <a name="NetworkInterface" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkInterface"></a>

Unified Azure Network Interface implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that replaces all
version-specific Network Interface classes. It automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining
full backward compatibility.

*Example*

```typescript
// Usage with explicit version pinning:
const nic = new NetworkInterface(this, "nic", {
  name: "mynic",
  location: "eastus",
  resourceGroupId: resourceGroup.id,
  ipConfigurations: [{
    name: "ipconfig1",
    subnet: { id: subnet.id },
    privateIPAllocationMethod: "Dynamic",
    primary: true
  }],
  apiVersion: "2024-07-01",
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkInterface.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { NetworkInterface } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

NetworkInterface.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkInterface.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### NetworkInterface <a name="NetworkInterface" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_networkinterface.NetworkInterface"></a>

Unified Azure Network Interface implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that replaces all
version-specific Network Interface classes. It automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining
full backward compatibility.

*Example*

```typescript
// Usage with explicit version pinning:
const nic = new NetworkInterface(this, "nic", {
  name: "mynic",
  location: "eastus",
  resourceGroupId: resourceGroup.id,
  ipConfigurations: [{
    name: "ipconfig1",
    subnet: { id: subnet.id },
    privateIPAllocationMethod: "Dynamic",
    primary: true
  }],
  apiVersion: "2024-07-01",
});
```

### NetworkSecurityGroup <a name="NetworkSecurityGroup" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkSecurityGroup"></a>

Azure Network Security Group implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that replaces
version-specific Network Security Group classes. It automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining
full backward compatibility.

*Example*

```typescript
// Usage with explicit version pinning:
const nsg = new NetworkSecurityGroup(this, "nsg", {
  name: "my-nsg",
  location: "eastus",
  apiVersion: "2024-07-01",
  securityRules: [...]
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkSecurityGroup.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { NetworkSecurityGroup } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

NetworkSecurityGroup.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkSecurityGroup.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### NetworkSecurityGroup <a name="NetworkSecurityGroup" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_networksecuritygroup.NetworkSecurityGroup"></a>

Azure Network Security Group implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that replaces
version-specific Network Security Group classes. It automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining
full backward compatibility.

*Example*

```typescript
// Usage with explicit version pinning:
const nsg = new NetworkSecurityGroup(this, "nsg", {
  name: "my-nsg",
  location: "eastus",
  apiVersion: "2024-07-01",
  securityRules: [...]
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_networksecuritygroup.NetworkSecurityGroup.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_networksecuritygroup } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_networksecuritygroup.NetworkSecurityGroup.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_networksecuritygroup.NetworkSecurityGroup.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### NetworkWatcher <a name="NetworkWatcher" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkWatcher"></a>

Unified Azure Network Watcher implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining full JSII compliance.

Network Watcher is a regional service that provides tools to monitor, diagnose, and gain
insights into your network health and performance in Azure. It serves as the anchor for
Network Watcher features like Flow Logs, Connection Monitor, and Packet Capture.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: Azure only allows one Network Watcher per subscription per region.
If you need Network Watcher functionality in multiple regions, you must create a separate
Network Watcher for each region.

*Example*

```typescript
// Network Watcher for use with Flow Logs:
const networkWatcher = new NetworkWatcher(this, "network-watcher", {
  name: "NetworkWatcher_eastus",
  location: "eastus",
  resourceGroupId: networkWatcherRg.id,
});

// Then use it with NSG Flow Logs
const flowLog = new NsgFlowLog(this, "flow-log", {
  networkWatcherId: networkWatcher.id,
  // ... other properties
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkWatcher.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { NetworkWatcher } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

NetworkWatcher.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.NetworkWatcher.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### NetworkWatcher <a name="NetworkWatcher" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_networkwatcher.NetworkWatcher"></a>

Unified Azure Network Watcher implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining full JSII compliance.

Network Watcher is a regional service that provides tools to monitor, diagnose, and gain
insights into your network health and performance in Azure. It serves as the anchor for
Network Watcher features like Flow Logs, Connection Monitor, and Packet Capture.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: Azure only allows one Network Watcher per subscription per region.
If you need Network Watcher functionality in multiple regions, you must create a separate
Network Watcher for each region.

*Example*

```typescript
// Network Watcher for use with Flow Logs:
const networkWatcher = new NetworkWatcher(this, "network-watcher", {
  name: "NetworkWatcher_eastus",
  location: "eastus",
  resourceGroupId: networkWatcherRg.id,
});

// Then use it with NSG Flow Logs
const flowLog = new NsgFlowLog(this, "flow-log", {
  networkWatcherId: networkWatcher.id,
  // ... other properties
});
```

### PolicyAssignment <a name="PolicyAssignment" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicyAssignment"></a>

Unified Azure Policy Assignment implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation for managing Azure
Policy Assignments. It automatically handles version resolution, schema validation,
and property transformation.

Note: Policy assignments can be deployed at management group, subscription, resource group,
or resource scope. Like policy definitions, they do not have a location property as they
are not region-specific.

*Example*

```typescript
// Policy assignment at management group scope:
const mgAssignment = new PolicyAssignment(this, "mgAssignment", {
  name: "mg-policy-assignment",
  policyDefinitionId: "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions/policy-id",
  scope: "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/my-mg",
  displayName: "Management Group Policy",
  description: "Applies policy across the entire management group hierarchy"
});
```

##### `addTag` <a name="addTag" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicyAssignment.addTag"></a>

```typescript
public addTag(key: string, value: string): void
```

Adds a tag to this resource. The tag will be included in the Azure resource.

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicyAssignment.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PolicyAssignment } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PolicyAssignment.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicyAssignment.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### PolicyAssignment <a name="PolicyAssignment" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_policyassignment.PolicyAssignment"></a>

Unified Azure Policy Assignment implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation for managing Azure
Policy Assignments. It automatically handles version resolution, schema validation,
and property transformation.

Note: Policy assignments can be deployed at management group, subscription, resource group,
or resource scope. Like policy definitions, they do not have a location property as they
are not region-specific.

*Example*

```typescript
// Policy assignment at management group scope:
const mgAssignment = new PolicyAssignment(this, "mgAssignment", {
  name: "mg-policy-assignment",
  policyDefinitionId: "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions/policy-id",
  scope: "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/my-mg",
  displayName: "Management Group Policy",
  description: "Applies policy across the entire management group hierarchy"
});
```

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.

the deployed Azure resource.

construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_policyassignment.PolicyAssignment.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_policyassignment } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_policyassignment.PolicyAssignment.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_policyassignment.PolicyAssignment.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PolicyDefinition <a name="PolicyDefinition" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicyDefinition"></a>

Unified Azure Policy Definition implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation for managing Azure
Policy Definitions. It automatically handles version resolution, schema validation,
and property transformation.

Note: Policy definitions are deployed at subscription or management group scope.
Unlike most Azure resources, they do not have a location property as they are
not region-specific.

*Example*

```typescript
// Policy definition at management group scope:
const mgPolicyDefinition = new PolicyDefinition(this, "mgPolicy", {
  name: "mg-require-tag-policy",
  parentId: "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/my-mg",
  displayName: "Management Group Tag Policy",
  description: "Enforces tags across the management group hierarchy",
  policyRule: {
    if: {
      field: "tags['CostCenter']",
      exists: "false"
    },
    then: {
      effect: "deny"
    }
  }
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicyDefinition.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PolicyDefinition } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PolicyDefinition.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicyDefinition.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### PolicyDefinition <a name="PolicyDefinition" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_policydefinition.PolicyDefinition"></a>

Unified Azure Policy Definition implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation for managing Azure
Policy Definitions. It automatically handles version resolution, schema validation,
and property transformation.

Note: Policy definitions are deployed at subscription or management group scope.
Unlike most Azure resources, they do not have a location property as they are
not region-specific.

*Example*

```typescript
// Policy definition at management group scope:
const mgPolicyDefinition = new PolicyDefinition(this, "mgPolicy", {
  name: "mg-require-tag-policy",
  parentId: "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/my-mg",
  displayName: "Management Group Tag Policy",
  description: "Enforces tags across the management group hierarchy",
  policyRule: {
    if: {
      field: "tags['CostCenter']",
      exists: "false"
    },
    then: {
      effect: "deny"
    }
  }
});
```

### PolicySetDefinition <a name="PolicySetDefinition" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicySetDefinition"></a>

Unified Azure Policy Set Definition (Initiative) implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation for managing Azure
Policy Set Definitions. It automatically handles version resolution, schema validation,
and property transformation.

Policy Set Definitions allow you to group multiple policy definitions together
and assign them as a single unit (also known as "Initiatives" in Azure Portal).

Note: Policy set definitions are created at subscription or management group scope.
They do not have a location property as they are not region-specific.

*Example*

```typescript
const initiative = new PolicySetDefinition(this, "security-initiative", {
  displayName: "Security Baseline",
  scope: "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  policyDefinitions: [
    {
      policyDefinitionId: "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions/abc123",
      policyDefinitionReferenceId: "auditVMsWithoutExtensions",
    },
  ],
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicySetDefinition.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PolicySetDefinition } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PolicySetDefinition.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PolicySetDefinition.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_policysetdefinition.PolicySetDefinition.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_policysetdefinition } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_policysetdefinition.PolicySetDefinition.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_policysetdefinition.PolicySetDefinition.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsAaaaRecord <a name="PrivateDnsAaaaRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsAaaaRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS AAAA Record implementation.

AAAA records map a hostname to one or more IPv6 addresses.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create an AAAA record:
const aaaaRecord = new PrivateDnsAaaaRecord(this, "web-aaaa-record", {
  name: "www",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 300,
  records: [
    { ipv6Address: "2001:db8::1" },
  ],
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsAaaaRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PrivateDnsAaaaRecord } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PrivateDnsAaaaRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsAaaaRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsAaaaRecord <a name="PrivateDnsAaaaRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsAaaaRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS AAAA Record implementation.

AAAA records map a hostname to one or more IPv6 addresses.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create an AAAA record:
const aaaaRecord = new PrivateDnsAaaaRecord(this, "web-aaaa-record", {
  name: "www",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 300,
  records: [
    { ipv6Address: "2001:db8::1" },
  ],
});
```


Adds a tag to this resource. The tag will be included in the Azure resource.

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

### PrivateDnsARecord <a name="PrivateDnsARecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsARecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS A Record implementation.

A records map a hostname to one or more IPv4 addresses.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create an A record with multiple IP addresses:
const aRecord = new PrivateDnsARecord(this, "web-a-record", {
  name: "www",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 300,
  records: [
    { ipv4Address: "10.0.1.4" },
    { ipv4Address: "10.0.1.5" },
  ],
});
```

Adds a tag to this resource. The tag will be included in the Azure resource.

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsARecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PrivateDnsARecord } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PrivateDnsARecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsARecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsARecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsARecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsARecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsCnameRecord <a name="PrivateDnsCnameRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsCnameRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS CNAME Record implementation.

CNAME records create an alias from one hostname to another.
Note: CNAME records cannot coexist with other record types at the same name.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create a CNAME record:
const cnameRecord = new PrivateDnsCnameRecord(this, "alias-record", {
  name: "app",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  cname: "www.internal.example.com",
});
```

### PrivateDnsCnameRecord <a name="PrivateDnsCnameRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsCnameRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS CNAME Record implementation.

CNAME records create an alias from one hostname to another.
Note: CNAME records cannot coexist with other record types at the same name.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create a CNAME record:
const cnameRecord = new PrivateDnsCnameRecord(this, "alias-record", {
  name: "app",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  cname: "www.internal.example.com",
});
```

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsCnameRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsCnameRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsCnameRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsMxRecord <a name="PrivateDnsMxRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsMxRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS MX Record implementation.

MX records specify mail exchange servers for a domain.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create an MX record:
const mxRecord = new PrivateDnsMxRecord(this, "mail-record", {
  name: "@",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  records: [
    { preference: 10, exchange: "mail1.internal.example.com" },
    { preference: 20, exchange: "mail2.internal.example.com" },
  ],
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsMxRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PrivateDnsMxRecord } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PrivateDnsMxRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsMxRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsMxRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsMxRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsMxRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### PrivateDnsPtrRecord <a name="PrivateDnsPtrRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsPtrRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS PTR Record implementation.

PTR records are used for reverse DNS lookups, mapping IP addresses to hostnames.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create a PTR record:
const ptrRecord = new PrivateDnsPtrRecord(this, "ptr-record", {
  name: "4.1.0.10.in-addr.arpa",
  privateDnsZoneId: reverseZone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  records: [
    { ptrdname: "server1.internal.example.com" },
  ],
});
```

### PrivateDnsPtrRecord <a name="PrivateDnsPtrRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsPtrRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS PTR Record implementation.

PTR records are used for reverse DNS lookups, mapping IP addresses to hostnames.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create a PTR record:
const ptrRecord = new PrivateDnsPtrRecord(this, "ptr-record", {
  name: "4.1.0.10.in-addr.arpa",
  privateDnsZoneId: reverseZone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  records: [
    { ptrdname: "server1.internal.example.com" },
  ],
});
```

Adds a tag to this resource. The tag will be included in the Azure resource.

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsPtrRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsPtrRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsPtrRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsSoaRecord <a name="PrivateDnsSoaRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsSoaRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS SOA Record implementation.

SOA records contain administrative information about a DNS zone.
Note: Each zone automatically has an SOA record; this is typically used to update it.

*Example*

```typescript
// Update the SOA record:
const soaRecord = new PrivateDnsSoaRecord(this, "soa-record", {
  name: "@",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  soaRecord: {
    email: "admin.example.com",
    refreshTime: 3600,
    retryTime: 300,
    expireTime: 2419200,
    minimumTtl: 300,
  },
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsSoaRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PrivateDnsSoaRecord } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PrivateDnsSoaRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsSoaRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsSoaRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsSoaRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsSoaRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsSrvRecord <a name="PrivateDnsSrvRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsSrvRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS SRV Record implementation.

SRV records specify the location of services like SIP, XMPP, etc.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create an SRV record for a SIP service:
const srvRecord = new PrivateDnsSrvRecord(this, "sip-record", {
  name: "_sip._tcp",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  records: [
    { priority: 10, weight: 60, port: 5060, target: "sipserver1.internal.example.com" },
    { priority: 10, weight: 40, port: 5060, target: "sipserver2.internal.example.com" },
  ],
});
```


Adds a tag to this resource. The tag will be included in the Azure resource.

This method provides proper immutability by storing tags separately from props.
Tags added via this method are combined with tags from props and included in
the deployed Azure resource.

**Important:** In CDK for Terraform, tags should ideally be set during resource
construction via props. While this method allows adding tags after construction,
those tags are only included if added before the Terraform configuration is
synthesized. For best results, add all tags via props or call addTag() in the
same scope where the resource is created.

### PrivateDnsSrvRecord <a name="PrivateDnsSrvRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsSrvRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS SRV Record implementation.

SRV records specify the location of services like SIP, XMPP, etc.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create an SRV record for a SIP service:
const srvRecord = new PrivateDnsSrvRecord(this, "sip-record", {
  name: "_sip._tcp",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  records: [
    { priority: 10, weight: 60, port: 5060, target: "sipserver1.internal.example.com" },
    { priority: 10, weight: 40, port: 5060, target: "sipserver2.internal.example.com" },
  ],
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsSrvRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsSrvRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsSrvRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsTxtRecord <a name="PrivateDnsTxtRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsTxtRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS TXT Record implementation.

TXT records store arbitrary text data, commonly used for SPF, DKIM, etc.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create a TXT record for SPF:
const txtRecord = new PrivateDnsTxtRecord(this, "spf-record", {
  name: "@",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  records: [
    { value: ["v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all"] },
  ],
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsTxtRecord.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PrivateDnsTxtRecord } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PrivateDnsTxtRecord.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsTxtRecord.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsTxtRecord <a name="PrivateDnsTxtRecord" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsTxtRecord"></a>

Azure Private DNS TXT Record implementation.

TXT records store arbitrary text data, commonly used for SPF, DKIM, etc.

*Example*

```typescript
// Create a TXT record for SPF:
const txtRecord = new PrivateDnsTxtRecord(this, "spf-record", {
  name: "@",
  privateDnsZoneId: zone.id,
  ttl: 3600,
  records: [
    { value: ["v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all"] },
  ],
});
```

### PrivateDnsZone <a name="PrivateDnsZone" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsZone"></a>

Unified Azure Private DNS Zone implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that replaces all
version-specific Private DNS Zone classes. It automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining
full backward compatibility.

Azure Private DNS Zones are used to provide internal DNS resolution within
Azure virtual networks. They enable name resolution for resources within a
virtual network without requiring custom DNS servers.

*Example*

```typescript
// Private DNS zone with explicit version pinning:
const privateDnsZone = new PrivateDnsZone(this, "privateDns", {
  name: "internal.contoso.com",
  location: "global",
  resourceGroupId: resourceGroup.id,
  apiVersion: "2024-06-01",
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsZone.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PrivateDnsZone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PrivateDnsZone.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsZone.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsZone <a name="PrivateDnsZone" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsZone"></a>

Unified Azure Private DNS Zone implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that replaces all
version-specific Private DNS Zone classes. It automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining
full backward compatibility.

Azure Private DNS Zones are used to provide internal DNS resolution within
Azure virtual networks. They enable name resolution for resources within a
virtual network without requiring custom DNS servers.

*Example*

```typescript
// Private DNS zone with explicit version pinning:
const privateDnsZone = new PrivateDnsZone(this, "privateDns", {
  name: "internal.contoso.com",
  location: "global",
  resourceGroupId: resourceGroup.id,
  apiVersion: "2024-06-01",
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsZone.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszone } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsZone.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszone.PrivateDnsZone.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsZoneLink <a name="PrivateDnsZoneLink" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsZoneLink"></a>

Azure Private DNS Zone Virtual Network Link implementation.

Virtual Network Links connect private DNS zones to virtual networks, enabling DNS
resolution from those VNets. They support auto-registration of VM DNS records and
configurable resolution policies.

*Example*

```typescript
// Virtual network link with resolution policy:
const link = new PrivateDnsZoneLink(this, "vnet-link", {
  name: "my-vnet-link",
  privateDnsZoneId: privateDnsZone.id,
  virtualNetworkId: vnet.id,
  resolutionPolicy: "NxDomainRedirect",
  location: "global",
  apiVersion: "2024-06-01"
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsZoneLink.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PrivateDnsZoneLink } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PrivateDnsZoneLink.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PrivateDnsZoneLink.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PrivateDnsZoneLink <a name="PrivateDnsZoneLink" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszonelink.PrivateDnsZoneLink"></a>

Azure Private DNS Zone Virtual Network Link implementation.

Virtual Network Links connect private DNS zones to virtual networks, enabling DNS
resolution from those VNets. They support auto-registration of VM DNS records and
configurable resolution policies.

*Example*

```typescript
// Virtual network link with resolution policy:
const link = new PrivateDnsZoneLink(this, "vnet-link", {
  name: "my-vnet-link",
  privateDnsZoneId: privateDnsZone.id,
  virtualNetworkId: vnet.id,
  resolutionPolicy: "NxDomainRedirect",
  location: "global",
  apiVersion: "2024-06-01"
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszonelink.PrivateDnsZoneLink.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_privatednszonelink } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_privatednszonelink.PrivateDnsZoneLink.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_privatednszonelink.PrivateDnsZoneLink.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PublicIPAddress <a name="PublicIPAddress" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PublicIPAddress"></a>

Azure Public IP Address implementation.

This class provides a single, version-aware implementation that replaces
version-specific Public IP Address classes. It automatically handles version
resolution, schema validation, and property transformation while maintaining
full backward compatibility.

*Example*

```typescript
// Zonal Public IP:
const publicIp = new PublicIPAddress(this, "publicIp", {
  name: "my-public-ip",
  location: "eastus",
  sku: {
    name: "Standard"
  },
  publicIPAllocationMethod: "Static",
  zones: ["1"]
});
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PublicIPAddress.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { PublicIPAddress } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

PublicIPAddress.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.PublicIPAddress.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_publicipaddress.PublicIPAddress.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { azure_publicipaddress } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

azure_publicipaddress.PublicIPAddress.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.azure_publicipaddress.PublicIPAddress.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.Resource.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { Resource } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

Resource.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.Resource.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.core_azure.Resource.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { core_azure } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

core_azure.Resource.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.core_azure.Resource.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.ResourceAction.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { ResourceAction } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

ResourceAction.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.ResourceAction.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.core_azure.ResourceAction.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { core_azure } from '@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs'

core_azure.ResourceAction.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@microsoft/terraform-cdk-constructs.core_azure.ResourceAction.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---
